claims.text: An integrated machine-learning and CALPHAD workflow can rapidly design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEAs.
CALPHAD can predict phase equilibria in the refractory multi-principal-element composition space.
Machine learning, such as Bayesian optimization, can narrow the candidate composition space based on predicted mechanical properties.
Screening at service-relevant simulation temperatures ensures phase stability under operational thermal conditions.
Screening at service-relevant simulation temperatures ensures mechanical performance under operational thermal conditions.
CALPHAD modeling can predict phase distributions and microstructural features such as fine precipitates or single-phase solid solutions.
Machine learning rapidly identifies promising regions of the RHEA compositional space by learning from computed thermodynamic and mechanical-property data.
CALPHAD ensures that candidate RHEA compositions are thermodynamically feasible.
Combining machine learning with CALPHAD accelerates discovery of compositions that balance strength, ductility, and low weight.
The integrated workflow will dramatically reduce the RHEA composition search space.
Experimentally validated candidates from the integrated workflow will exhibit significantly improved strength and ductility relative to alloys designed using traditional methods.
Candidates from the integrated workflow will have lower density than alloys designed using traditional thermokinetic and simulation methods.
Conventional design methods based on detailed thermokinetic analysis and exhaustive simulation are computationally intensive.
Conventional design methods are slower at narrowing candidate compositions than the proposed integrated workflow.
Limited experimental data and modeling assumptions create uncertainty in quantitative mechanical-property predictions.
The integrated approach may be less effective for compositions containing exotic or unrepresented local atomic configurations.
